figures.caption: Fig. 1. Overview of BAT-CLIP. A trainable brain encoder fθ, initialized from brain foundation model DIVER-1, maps neural windows to brain embeddings zB . Frozen AudioCLIP encoders provide audio anchors zA and text anchors zT . BAT-CLIP optimizes a trimodal contrastive objective LTotal to align neural embeddings with the joint audio–text representation space.

Table 1. Overall decoding performance (averaged over 9 subjects). We report AUC for Content, Onset, POS, GPT surprisal, and Word Emb decoding, and accuracy for Whisper. ∆ denotes relative gain over the supervised CNN baseline (baseline ∆: “–”). † indicates full fine-tuning (CNN); all other methods are evaluated via linear probing. BA-CLIP, BT-CLIP, and BAT-CLIP apply CLIP-style contrastive alignment on top of the pretrained DIVER-1 brain encoder, using brain–audio, brain– text, and trimodal brain–audio–text alignment, respectively. Overall, DIVER-1 is the strongest foundation-model baseline, CLIP alignment generally improves over DIVER-1, and BAT-CLIP achieves the best result among the aligned variants on five of six probe tasks. Bold and underline denote the best and second-best results within each column.

Table 2. Effect of pretraining across methods. We compare CLIP-aligned models trained from scratch (Scratch) versus the same models initialized with pretrained DIVER-1 weights, across unimodal alignments (BA-CLIP: brain–audio; BT-CLIP: brain–text) and trimodal alignment (BAT-CLIP: brain–audio–text). As in Table 1, ∆ denotes relative gain over the supervised CNN baseline (baseline ∆: “–”). Pretrained DIVER-1 initialization is key to realizing the gains from trimodal CLIP alignment; training from scratch largely fails to capitalize on brain–audio–text supervision.

Fig. 2. Visualization of learned word-level representations. 2D t-SNE projection of brain embeddings extracted by various models for Sub03. Each point represents a single word-level embedding. The color of the point denotes the sentence to which the word belongs, and the shape indicates the speaker. Compared to the baselines, the proposed trimodal alignment model, BATCLIP, exhibits tighter clustering of words from the same sentence (shared colors), consistent with the sentence-level clustering results in Table 3.
